title: Decode a Run-Length Encoded List
required_features: A sound logical primitive or definable measure for integer-indexed repeat(n, x) that returns the exact ordered List containing n copies of x; Synquid measures structurally recurse on a declared datatype, not on the int carried by Many.
A way to use the exact result of a typed helper such as repeat in a refinement/measure equation. Ordinary Synquid function signatures cannot be invoked as logical predicates or measures.
Alternatively, an equivalent sound inductive relation over an Int run count, an element, and an ordered output List that can be defined and used in the refinement language.
semantic_obligations: Many (n, x) expands to n consecutive x values on the source-valid generated-code domain.
Expansion preserves segment encounter order and every occurrence; neither sets nor lengths alone are adequate.
The official example must yield exactly the stated fourteen-element string list.
No behavior is invented for manually constructed Many counts that fall outside the source-referenced encoder's unstated invariant.
notes: No contract.sq or synthesis logs were produced. A bounded pinned-runtime probe confirmed that List-valued measures and equality can retain order, but the required exact integer-indexed repeat relation is unavailable: measures structurally recurse on datatype inputs, and ordinary typed helper functions cannot occur in logical measure bodies. A weak length/set contract was deliberately not run. Independent standard-library-only OCaml tests cover the official example, edge cases, and exhaustive positive-count small codes; an explicitly incorrect stub was compiled against them and failed the expected semantic assertion.
